summary: The note summarizes the Economy of India as a developing mixed economy that ranks among the world's largest by nominal GDP and by purchasing power parity. It gives per capita GDP rankings for 2016 and notes average growth of 6-7% annually after the 1991 liberalisation. It also reports that India's economy became the fastest growing major economy in FY 2015 (and 2017), surpassing China, and attributes its positive long-term prospects to demographics, savings and investment rates, and global integration. The three passages are overlapping versions of the same text that differ slightly in wording, such as sixth versus seventh largest by nominal GDP.
one_line: Overview of India's developing mixed economy, its GDP rankings, post-1991 liberalisation growth, and long-term prospects.
key_facts: India's economy is a developing mixed economy.
India is the world's sixth-largest economy by nominal GDP and the third-largest by purchasing power parity (PPP).
One version of the note calls India the world's seventh-largest economy by nominal GDP.
India ranks 141st in per capita GDP (nominal) with $1723 as of 2016.
India ranks 123rd in per capita GDP (PPP) with $6,616 as of 2016.
After 1991 economic liberalisation, India achieved 6-7% average GDP growth annually.
In FY 2015 and 2017, India's economy became the world's fastest growing major economy, surpassing China.
One version of the note mentions only FY 2015 for the fastest-growing milestone.
The long-term growth prospects of the Indian economy are positive.
Reasons for the positive growth outlook include a young population, a corresponding low dependency ratio, healthy savings and investment rates, and increasing integration into the global economy.
